preamble: Palatalization of the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] to the palatal glide [j], typically after or between front vowels. In Old English the Proto-Germanic fricative *g [ɣ] became [j] next to front vowels (dæġ [dæj] 'day' < *dagaz); in Danish the historical soft g [ɣ] became [j] after front vowels and /l/ (vej 'way' < Old Danish wægh); and Turkish ğ is realized as [j] between front vowels.

examples.note: After fronting of the vowel to æ, the fricative became the glide [j] (spelled ġ); Modern English 'day'.
The historical voiced velar fricative corresponds to [j] after front vowels and /l/, and to [w] after back vowels and /r/, in Standard Danish.
Between front vowels ğ is either silent or realized as [j], depending on the surrounding vowels.
